metaDescription: Six string trimmers under $75, corded and 20V cordless, compared on swath, motor, battery kits and weight so small yards get the right tool.
expertTake: The 13-inch BLACK+DECKER 4 amp corded unit is the reliable pick for a small yard near an outlet, and the 21V 12-inch with two 4Ah batteries is the best cordless kit for the money. The WEN compact is the best choice for shorter users. Skip this price band if you have a large yard or thick brush, because light 20V trimmers run out of battery and torque. Check the live price and listing before ordering.
introParagraphs: Under $75 you are buying a light-duty trimmer for edges, fence lines and small lawns. The real choice is between a corded motor that never runs down and a budget cordless kit with small batteries.

Spec sheets in this class lean on RPM and battery voltage, but torque, weight and what ships in the box matter more. Prices move and the $75 cap reflects listing prices when this guide was updated, so check the live number before buying.

products.name: 21V 12-Inch Cordless Trimmer Edger with Two 4Ah Batteries
products.description:
This cordless kit ships with two 4.0Ah batteries and a fast charger, which makes it the most complete package in the guide. Two packs of that capacity are worth far more than the two 2Ah packs that come with some rivals, because runtime scales with amp-hours and a 4Ah pack holds twice the energy at the same voltage. The 9500 RPM motor is a no-load figure, so treat it as a ceiling for light grass.

A 12-inch swath and a trimmer-to-edger conversion cover the usual small-yard jobs: lawn edges, fence lines and the strip along a driveway. Compared with the HEYWORK it has the faster motor claim and a lighter weight class, and compared with the corded units it trades unlimited runtime for freedom of movement.

Ownership is simple. Keep packs indoors, swap when one sags and replace the line before it wears short of the swath. The brand is unnamed in the listing, so keep your receipt and check the return window in the first month. Charge both packs after the season ends and store them half full, since a fully drained lithium pack left on a shelf loses capacity. Expect to buy replacement line before you need new batteries.
products.bestFor: Small yards without a convenient outlet.
cons: Packs are not interchangeable with big platforms

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 4A 13-Inch Corded String Trimmer
products.description:
The BLACK+DECKER corded trimmer uses a 4 amp motor to spin a 13-inch swath with automatic line feed. The auto-feed spool advances line without bumping the head on the ground, which saves effort on long edges. A built-in auxiliary handle improves balance and reduces wrist strain.

A corded motor never runs flat, so it will finish a job that would drain a 2Ah cordless kit. The cost is the cord: you need an outdoor extension and must keep it behind you. Compared with the 14-inch 6.5 amp BLACK+DECKER in this guide it is lighter and weaker, and compared with the WEN it has a wider swath and a more established parts channel.

The brand has a long track record, so replacement spools and parts are easy to find. Store the cord coiled loosely and replace line when it drops below swath length. Wear long pants and eye protection, because even a small corded head throws stones and twigs. Coil the cord loosely rather than wrapping it tight around the shaft, which cracks insulation over time.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 6.5A 14-Inch 2-in-1 Corded Trimmer Edger
products.description:
This is the strongest machine in the guide on paper: a 6.5 amp motor with a Powerdrive transmission that raises torque at the head. The swath is 14 inches, the widest here, and the head rotates to a wheeled edge guide for sidewalk and bed edging.

More amps help in thicker grass where the 3 and 4 amp units bog. Compared with the 4 amp BLACK+DECKER, it clears faster and handles heavier growth, at the cost of more weight. Compared with the cordless kits it does not run out of charge but it needs a cord.

Expect to use a 16-gauge or thicker outdoor cord and to replace line often, since the wider swath eats line faster. If your lawn is mostly flat, the wheel guide will keep the edge straight along a driveway. Keep the vents clear of grass clippings because the bigger motor produces more heat.
products.bestFor: Thicker grass and long edges near an outlet.

products.name: WEN ET1003 10-Inch Compact Corded String Trimmer
products.description:
The WEN ET1003 is built to be short and light: 4 pounds and 37.5 inches long. A 3 amp motor spins to 10,500 RPM and the automatic feed keeps line length consistent. That compact length makes it comfortable for shorter users and easy to store.

It is the least powerful machine here, with the narrowest swath at 10 inches, so it needs more passes. Compared with the 6.5 amp BLACK+DECKER it is a quarter of the torque in theory but far easier to carry.

It makes sense as a tool for tidying around a patio, balcony planters or small beds. Do not expect it to cut waist-high weeds. Because it is short, it is easy to hang on a garage hook and out of the way. Do not expect it to handle woody stems, and keep it away from damp grass that bogs the head.
products.bestFor: Shorter users and tight, light trimming jobs.

products.name: HEYWORK 20V 12-Inch Cordless Trimmer Edger Two 4Ah
products.description:
HEYWORK pairs a 20V platform with two 4Ah batteries, an 8000 RPM motor and automatic line feed. The 6.3-pound weight is on the heavy side for a cordless unit in this class because of the larger batteries. An adjustable grip helps reduce arm fatigue.

Compared with the 21V kit it has a slower motor claim, and compared with the 3.5-pound 20V unit in other guides it has more battery and more weight. The 4Ah packs are the real value.

It suits a yard of modest size where you want to work for 30 minutes at a time. With larger packs comes extra weight, so use the adjustable grip and switch hands occasionally. Check the head for wrapped grass after each tank of work.
products.bestFor: Moderate yards where battery size matters.
cons: 6.3 lb is heavy for the class

products.name: 21V Lightweight Cordless Trimmer Edger for Small Lawns
products.description:
This lightweight cordless model is marketed to small lawns and older users. It has a 9000 RPM motor, two 2Ah batteries with fast charging and a trimmer-to-edger switch.

With only 2Ah per pack, it holds half the energy of the 4Ah kits, so runtime is the compromise. Compared with the HEYWORK, it is lighter and cheaper but runs out sooner.

It is a sensible tidy-up tool for a tiny yard. Charge the batteries on a flat surface and do not leave them on the charger for weeks. This is a sensible machine for the person who trims for ten minutes a week.

buyingCriteria.explanation: The BLACK+DECKER 6.5A and 4A never run flat, but you drag a cord. The 21V and HEYWORK kits go anywhere but give about 20 to 40 minutes of light trimming per pack. If you can reach every edge from an outlet within about 100 feet, corded is the better value. Be honest about the longest run you trim in one go, then add 50 percent.

Two 4Ah packs hold twice the energy of two 2Ah packs at the same voltage. The 21V kit and the HEYWORK include 4Ah packs, while the lightweight 21V includes 2Ah. For a yard bigger than a postage stamp, capacity matters more than RPM. Check the charger rating too, since a slow charger leaves you waiting.

RPM is measured without load. The WEN claims 10,500 RPM on a 3 amp motor, but the 6.5 amp BLACK+DECKER with Powerdrive will cut thicker grass despite lower headline numbers. For thick growth, look at amps or transmission, not RPM. If the grass is wet or thick, a stronger motor saves the batteries.

A 14-inch swath cuts 40 percent more per pass than a 10-inch one. Wider heads need more torque, which budget motors lack. Match the swath to the motor: 12 to 13 inches is the practical sweet spot at this price. Try the balance by holding the shaft at the grip height you will use.

The WEN weighs 4 pounds and is 37.5 inches long, while the HEYWORK weighs 6.3 pounds. Over 30 minutes, an extra two pounds is noticeable. Shorter users should favor the compact WEN. Use a wire-free head cover when you store it.

Automatic feed, found on the BLACK+DECKER and WEN units, saves bumping. Convertible heads switch to edging for sidewalks. Check the line size before buying spares. Buy spare line when you buy the machine so you never run short.

specDecoder.meaning: Battery capacity. Double the Ah means roughly double the runtime at the same voltage. It is the most useful number on a cordless listing.
specDecoder.watchFor: The 21V kit and HEYWORK list 4Ah, the lightweight 21V lists 2Ah.

specDecoder.meaning: Head speed without cutting. Under load it drops, so it is a ceiling. A loaded motor spins slower.
Motor current draw. Higher amps mean more potential torque. Cord gauge matters at the upper end.
specDecoder.watchFor: The BLACK+DECKER units list 4 and 6.5 amp.

specDecoder.meaning: The cutting circle width. Wider cuts more per pass. Wide swaths need torque.
specDecoder.watchFor: The 14 in is widest, the WEN 10 in narrowest.

specDecoder.meaning: A transmission that boosts torque at the head. It lets a light motor cut thicker stems.

howToChoose.intro: Pick the row that matches the yard you really have, not the one you wish you had.
Prices here are close together, so the tiers show which extras you pay for.

cards.label: Corded
cards.text: The BLACK+DECKER 4A and 6.5A and the WEN never run out of charge and weigh little. A cord restricts range. They also have fewer parts to fail.

cards.label: Cordless
cards.text: The 21V kit, HEYWORK and lightweight 21V go anywhere. Packs limit runtime and cost more. They suit awkward corners far from the house.

howToChoose.note: Pick corded if an outlet is near; cordless if not.

howToChoose.intro: Weight decides how long you will enjoy the job.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A straight shaft and a head that tilts or rotates, so you can reach under rails. Keep the head angle shallow to avoid scalping the lawn.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The BLACK+DECKER 6.5A rotates to edge, and the 21V kit pivots. The WEN is compact for tight spots. Mow first, then trim the fence line for the neatest result.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Your yard is over a quarter acre or has thick weeds. Move to a 40V or gas trimmer. A gas or 40V unit has the torque for heavy growth.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You trim a small patch. The WEN or BLACK+DECKER 4A is plenty. Spend the difference on spare line and eye protection.

maintenance.why: Short line cuts a smaller swath and strains the motor. It takes only a minute and prevents the most common complaints.

faq.a: For small yards and edges, yes. For thick weeds or large lawns they are too light. Keep expectations to light trimming and edging.
Corded for unlimited runtime, cordless for freedom. Choose by outlet distance. A cord of 14 to 16 gauge works for these motors.
About 20 to 40 minutes of light trimming on 2 to 4Ah packs. Cold weather shortens that further.

faq.q: Does higher RPM mean more power?
faq.a: No, it is a no-load figure. Torque matters more. A heavy-duty motor also has a gearbox.

faq.q: What line size do I need?
faq.a: Check the head. Many budget heads use 0.065 inch line. Thicker line can overload a light motor.

faq.q: How do I clear a tangled head?
faq.a: Unplug or remove the battery first, then cut away the wrap. Never reach for the head with the power connected.
